items.title: A Ground Transition at Last: The Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation Opens

items.zh: 已說思所成地。云何修所成地？
items.en:
Within the Basic Section, the twelfth ground: the Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation.
The Ground of What Is Attained Through Reflection has now been explained. What, then, is the Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation?

items.zh: 謂略由四處，當知普攝修所成地。何等四處？一者、修處所，二者、修因緣，三者、修瑜伽，四者、修果。如是四處，七支所攝。何等為七？一、生圓滿；二、聞正法圓滿；三、涅槃為上首；四、能熟解脫慧之成熟；五、修習對治；六、世間一切種清淨；七、出世間一切種清淨。如此四處七支所攝普聖教義，廣說應知。依善說法毘奈耶中，一切學處皆得圓滿。
items.en: That is, in brief, the Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation should be understood as comprehensively included under four topics. What are the four? First, the setting of cultivation; second, the causes and conditions of cultivation; third, the yoga of cultivation; fourth, the fruit of cultivation. These four topics are comprised in seven branches. What are the seven? First, a favourable rebirth-basis; second, complete access to hearing the true teaching; third, nirvāṇa held as the governing aim; fourth, the maturing of the wisdom that ripens liberation; fifth, cultivating the remedies; sixth, mundane purity of every kind; seventh, supramundane purity of every kind. The meaning of the whole noble teaching comprised in these four topics and seven branches should be understood in full. Within the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, every point of training is brought to completion.

items.title: The First Branch Opens: What Makes a Rebirth Genuinely Favourable

items.zh: 云何生圓滿？當知略有十種。謂依內有五，依外有五，總依內外合有十種。
items.en: What is a favourable rebirth-basis? It should be known that, in brief, there are ten kinds: five belonging to one's own person, and five belonging to external circumstance — ten altogether, internal and external combined.

items.zh: 云何生圓滿中依內有五？
items.en: What are the five that belong to one's own person within a favourable rebirth-basis?

items.title: The Five Internal Conditions of a Favourable Rebirth

items.zh: 謂眾同分圓滿、處所圓滿、依止圓滿、無業障圓滿、無信解障圓滿。
items.en: Namely: a favourable class of birth, a favourable place, a favourable bodily basis, freedom from karmic obstruction, and freedom from obstruction by wrong conviction.

items.zh: 眾同分圓滿者，謂如有一，生在人中，得丈夫身，男根成就。處所圓滿者，謂如有一，生在人中，又處中國，不生邊地。謂於是處有四眾行。謂苾芻、苾芻尼、近事男、近事女。不生達須、篾戾車中。謂於是處無四眾行，亦無賢聖、正至、正行、諸善丈夫。依止圓滿者，謂如有一，生處中國，不缺眼耳隨一支分，性不頑嚚，亦不瘖瘂，堪能解了善說、惡說所有法義。無業障圓滿者，謂如有一，依止圓滿，於五無間隨一業障，不自造作，不教他作。若有作此，於現身中，必非證得賢聖法器。無信解障圓滿者，謂如有一，必不成就五無間業，不於惡處而生信解，不於惡處發清淨心。謂於種種邪天處所，及於種種外道處所。由彼前生，於佛聖教善說法處，修習淨信，長時相續；由此因緣，於今生中，唯於聖處發生信解，起清淨心。云何生圓滿中依外有五？
items.en: A favourable class of birth means that a certain person is born among human beings, obtains a male body, and is endowed with the male faculty. A favourable place means that a certain person is born among human beings and, moreover, lives in the central country and is not born in a border region — that is, a place where the fourfold assembly is active: bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, laymen and laywomen; and is not born among the Dasyus or the Mlecchas — that is, places where the fourfold assembly is not active and where there are neither noble ones, nor those who have rightly arrived, nor those who rightly practise, nor any good persons. A favourable bodily basis means that a certain person, born in the central country, lacks none of the limbs such as eye or ear, is not dull-witted by nature, nor dumb, and is able to understand the meaning of teachings that are well spoken and ill spoken. Freedom from karmic obstruction means that a certain person, having a favourable bodily basis, has neither personally committed nor instigated others to commit any one of the five karmic obstructions of immediate retribution; for if one has done this, then in this present life one can certainly not become a vessel for attaining the Dharma of the noble ones. Freedom from obstruction by wrong conviction means that a certain person certainly does not possess the five deeds of immediate retribution, does not place conviction in wrong objects, and does not arouse a pure mind towards wrong objects — that is, towards the various shrines of false gods and the various places of non-Buddhist teachers. Because in former lives this person cultivated pure faith over a long, continuous period in the well-proclaimed Dharma of the Buddha's noble teaching, for this reason in the present life they place conviction only in what is noble and arouse a pure mind towards it alone. What are the five that belong to external circumstance within a favourable rebirth-basis?

items.title: The Five External Conditions of a Favourable Rebirth

items.zh: 謂大師圓滿、世俗正法施設圓滿、勝義正法隨轉圓滿、正行不滅圓滿、隨順資緣圓滿。
items.en: Namely: a perfected teacher, the conventional true teaching being fully articulated, the ultimate true teaching still being transmitted through living realisation, right practice not yet having died out, and favourable material support.

items.zh: 大師圓滿者，謂即彼補特伽羅，具內五種生圓滿已，復得值遇大師出世。所謂如來應正等覺、一切知者、一切見者，於一切境得無障礙。世俗正法施設圓滿者，謂即彼補特伽羅，值佛出世，又廣開示善不善法，有罪無罪，廣說乃至諸緣生法、及廣分別。謂契經、應頌、記別、諷誦、自說、緣起、譬喻、本事、本生、方廣、希法、及與論議。勝義正法隨轉圓滿者，謂即大師善為開示俗正法已；諸弟子眾依此正法，復得他人為說隨順教誡教授，修三十七菩提分法，得沙門果；於沙門果證得圓滿，又能證得展轉勝上增長廣大所有功德。正行不滅圓滿者，謂佛世尊雖般涅槃；而俗正法、猶住未滅，勝義正法未隱未斷。隨順資緣圓滿者，謂即四種受用正法因緣現前，受用正法。諸有正信長者、居士、婆羅門等，知彼受用正法而轉，恐乏資緣，退失如是所受正法，是故慇懃奉施種種衣服、飲食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥供身什物。如是十種，名依內外生圓滿。即此十種生圓滿，名修瑜伽處所。由此所依、所建立處為依止故，證得如來諸弟子眾所有聖法。如是聖法，略有二種。一、有學法，二、無學法。今此義中，意取無學所有聖法。謂無學正見，廣說乃至無學正智。何以故？由諸有學雖有聖法，而相續中，非聖煩惱之所隨逐現可得故。如是初支生圓滿廣聖教義，有此十種。除此、更無餘生圓滿，若過若增。
items.en: A perfected teacher means that this very person, already endowed with the five internal kinds of favourable rebirth-basis, further meets with the appearance in the world of the great Teacher — namely the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the all-knowing one, the all-seeing one, unobstructed with regard to every object. The conventional true teaching being fully articulated means that this very person meets a Buddha who has appeared in the world and who, moreover, extensively reveals what is wholesome and unwholesome, what is blameworthy and blameless, and so on in full, up to dependently arisen phenomena, together with their extensive analysis — namely the discourses, the mixed prose and verse, the expositions, the verses, the inspired utterances, the occasions, the parables, the accounts of past events, the birth stories, the extensive teachings, the marvels, and the treatises. The ultimate true teaching still being transmitted means that, once the great Teacher has well revealed the conventional true teaching, the assembly of disciples, relying on this true teaching, further obtain from others instruction and guidance in accordance with it; they cultivate the thirty-seven factors of awakening and attain the fruits of the ascetic life; they bring the attainment of those fruits to completion, and are also able to attain qualities that become progressively more excellent, growing and expanding. Right practice not yet having died out means that, although the Buddha, the Blessed One, has entered parinirvāṇa, the conventional true teaching still remains and has not perished, and the ultimate true teaching has not been hidden or cut off. Favourable material support means that the four kinds of causes and conditions for making use of the true teaching are present, and the true teaching is made use of. Elders, householders, brahmins and others who have right faith, knowing that these people live by making use of the true teaching, and fearing that, should they lack material support, they might fall away from the teaching they have received, therefore earnestly offer them clothing, food and drink, bedding and seats, medicine for illness, and other requisites for the body. These ten kinds are called the favourable rebirth-basis dependent on internal and external factors. These same ten kinds of favourable rebirth-basis are called the setting for the cultivation of yoga. By relying on this as the basis and as the ground on which things are established, the Tathāgata's assembly of disciples attain all the noble qualities. These noble qualities are, in brief, of two kinds: first, the qualities of those in training; second, the qualities of those beyond training. In the present meaning, the intention is to take the noble qualities of those beyond training — namely the right view of one beyond training, and so on in full, up to the right knowledge of one beyond training. Why is this? Because, although those in training have noble qualities, it is still found that their mental continuum is followed by afflictions that are not noble. Thus the meaning of the noble teaching in full concerning the first branch, the favourable rebirth-basis, consists of these ten kinds. Beyond these, there is no further favourable rebirth-basis to exceed them, and none further to add.

blocks.text: The twelfth stage, the **Stage Attained Through Cultivation** (修所成地), fills a single fascicle. After hearing (Stage 10) and reflection (Stage 11) comes cultivation: meditative practice that transforms. Master Cháng Bǎi: all three vehicles pass through hearing, reflection, and cultivation. Several definitions are missing from Ru-Yi's translation; the English column gives our own translation, marked as ours, and the commentary summarises them.

The stage is organised under four headings: the **place** of cultivation, its **causes**, the **practice** itself, and its **fruit**. These are unfolded as seven branches: (1) favourable birth, (2) full access to hearing the true teaching, (3) nirvāṇa as the governing aim, (4) ripening of liberating wisdom, (5) cultivating the remedies, (6) mundane purity of every kind, (7) supramundane purity of every kind.
Favourable birth has ten conditions, five inner and five outer: the "place" in which yoga can be practised.

**Inner** (definitions missing from Ru-Yi's translation, 0388b22): born human; in a "central land", where the fourfold assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen is found (Master Cháng Bǎi: "so Taiwan is a central land"), not among peoples where no noble ones live; with sound faculties and a mind able to understand good and bad teaching; free of the five heinous deeds; and with faith directed only to the right place, the fruit of faith cultivated in former lives. Master Cháng Bǎi: the human body, half pleasure and half pain, is most suitable for practice; hell beings have no time, gods too much pleasure.

**Outer** (0388c13): a Buddha has appeared; the conventional teaching has been fully set out in the twelve divisions of scripture; the ultimate teaching continues, as disciples practise and attain the fruits; right practice has not died out after the Buddha's passing; and faithful householders provide robes, food, bedding, and medicine, so that practitioners need not lack. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you must work for a living, you will have neither energy nor time for the Dharma.

These ten are the "place of yoga". On this basis the noble qualities of those beyond training are attained: right view through right knowledge. The treatise ends each branch with a formula: "there are these ten; there is nothing beyond them, neither more nor less."
Every condition is outside our control except, perhaps, the last two inner ones. The list is a reminder that the chance to practise is itself the fruit of many causes, and is rare.

quiz.q: Which ground of the Basic Section is the Ground of Cultivation, and which ground does it follow?
options: the thirteenth, after the śrāvaka ground
the tenth, after the mindless ground
quiz.why: "Within the Basic Section, the twelfth ground: the Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation. The Ground of Reflection has now been explained." Master Cháng Bǎi: the three grounds of hearing, reflection, and cultivation are a process every practitioner of the three vehicles must pass through.

quiz.q: Is the Ground of Cultivation meant only for śrāvakas, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the three grounds are common to all three vehicles; even Mahāyāna practitioners must pass through them and know the śrāvaka path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the three grounds of hearing, reflection, and cultivation are a process all three vehicles must pass through; even Mahāyāna practitioners seeking unsurpassed awakening must go through them and become familiar with the śrāvaka path.

quiz.q: How many kinds of favourable basis does the treatise list, and how are they divided?
quiz.why: "In brief, there are ten kinds: five belonging to one's own person, and five belonging to external circumstance — ten altogether." Venerable Miào Jìng: "internal" means five things in the practitioner being taught.

quiz.q: In "freedom from karmic obstruction," what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the karmic obstruction is?
options: the five acts of immediate retribution — not ordinary karma, which can be purified by repentance
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the karmic obstruction here means the five acts of immediate retribution, not ordinary karma; ordinary karma can be purified through repentance, and one can still practice the noble path.

quiz.q: "A favourable place" means being born in the "central land." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: wherever the fourfold assembly of Buddhists lives is the central land
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: wherever the fourfold Buddhist assembly lives, that place is the "central land" — so Taiwan is a central land.

quiz.q: "A favourable class of birth" means a human body. Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi, is it best for practice?
options: human life has pleasure and pain in balance; hell beings only suffer, gods enjoy too much
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the human body, half pleasure and half pain, is most suitable for practice; hell beings receive only pain and have no time; gods' sensual pleasure is too strong for them to practise.

quiz.q: How do the masters distinguish the conventional true teaching from the ultimate teaching "transmitted"?
options: Miào Jìng: the conventional teaching is the Dharma in words; Cháng Bǎi: transmission is realised practitioners passing on their realisation, mind to mind
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the conventional true teaching is the Dharma in language and writing. Master Cháng Bǎi: when someone realises the noble path and passes on that experience, it is called transmission — turning the Dharma wheel from teacher's mind to disciples' minds, mind sealing mind.
